messages:
Anna L.: quick one — SDK pagination + retries across runtime fallback (hosted -> dedicated -> private). do we preserve the same cursor/token semantics, or do we treat a runtime switch as a hard reset?
Diego R.: my instinct: keep cursor opaque and server-driven. client should never assume stability across model variants. treat runtime switch as potentially non-resumable unless server says otherwise.
Priya S.: agree, but product wants seamless failover for long listings (users expect no manual resume). can server annotate cursor with "resumable":true?
Anna L.: yes that's an option. question is what the SDK should do when it sees a transient error and the router switches runtimes mid-stream. retry with idempotency keys? resume? backoff?
Kevin M.: propose 2-mode approach: "best-effort resume" and "strict transactional". default best-effort: SDK will attempt to resume using last cursor, with exponential backoff and a soft fallback to restarting from beginning (with a de-dup window on consumer). strict transactional: surface error to caller.
Diego R.: implementation detail: we need an idempotency token for server to dedupe items if restart occurs. otherwise clients will get dupes. server can return a monotonic sequence number per item as optional metadata.
Priya S.: could we rely on per-item ids for dedupe instead of global idempotency? less coupling to infra. many downstreams can dedupe by id.
Kevin M.: yes, but not all models/streams provide stable ids. for embeddings/payloads we might, but for some chat-like listing responses we won't.
Anna L.: what about transient vs fatal errors classification? SDK needs to know which to retry across runtimes.
Diego R.: classify: network + 5xx as retryable; 4xx except 429 as non-retryable. but special-case 409s if router indicates capacity move -> treat as retryable with longer window.
Priya S.: add a header in server hinting "runtime-switch-expected": true/false and "cursor-preserved": true/false. SDK can decide.
Anna L.: sample SDK flow: 1) list() -> yields page+cursor. 2) on error, check server hints. 3a) if cursor_preserved yes -> attempt resume up to N attempts with backoff. 3b) if no -> surface error OR restart from 0 depending on mode.
Kevin M.: propose default N=3, jittered exp backoff up to 8s, then try failover once to new runtime. telemetry event for each runtime hop.
Diego R.: small nit: when restarting from 0, we should allow caller to supply a de-dup handler or accept that SDK will remove items that match a seen-id set (bounded memory, LRU). document the memory tradeoffs.
Priya S.: docs + console should show per-route resume-compatibility matrix. product can gate which models/runtimes promise resumability.
Anna L.: SDK ergonomics: callers should be able to pass resume_strategy = ["resume","restart","fail"] and idempotency_key opt-in. default resume then restart. keep API same across py/ts/go.
Kevin M.: on surface: expose RetryPolicy object with backoff, max_attempts, resume_strategy. examples in quickstart.
sre-bot: deploy bot: routed 1955554321 -> dedicated-pool-07 during incident 2025-07-11T09:12Z (informational).
Diego R.: thanks for the signal. that infra event argues for making runtime hops visible to SDK logs so customers can debug pagination anomalies.
Anna L.: ok next steps: 1) Priya to spec server headers for cursor_preserved/runtime_hint. 2) Diego to add telemetry for runtime hops. 3) Kevin to sketch RetryPolicy API for py/ts/go. 4) I'll write a short RFC follow-up summarizing modes.
Priya S.: i'll drop a draft in #eng-platform tomorrow.
Kevin M.: i'll mock the client API in TS + Python this week. any objections to defaulting resume_strategy to "resume_then_restart"?
Diego R.: fine by me. just ensure docs warn about potential dupes without id fields.
Anna L.: perfect. :thumbsup:
